symptom: `column (attribute: FieldService.ServiceRequest_LithoSystem/SerialNumber)` in a Data grid 2 failed `mxcli check` with MDL-WIDGET34 (printing the value as `&{…}`, the column as "column ``", and advising to wrap it in a data view although it sat in a grid) plus MDL-WIDGET42 "cannot hold the expression"; the bare `ServiceRequest_LithoSystem/SerialNumber` passed. XPath and data view sources name the same association module-qualified, so the qualified spelling is the natural one.
cause: `attributePathV3` (MDLPage.g4) took only plain identifiers between slashes, so `Module.Assoc/Attr` missed `ATTRIBUTE COLON attributePathV3` and fell through to the generic `keyword COLON expression` alternative, parsing as the division `Module.Assoc / Attr` -> ast.WidgetExpressionV3. The executor already accepted qualified hops (resolveAssociationPathIn keeps a dotted name). The WIDGET34 message formatted the non-string value with %v and assumed a named widget outside any data container.
fix: Grammar: `attributePathV3 : (attributePathHopV3 SLASH)* attributePathSegmentV3`, a hop optionally `Module.Assoc`; the final segment stays bare so `M.E.A` (no slash) is not a path. buildAttributePathV3 unquotes each dotted part. Message: nonStringAttributeText returns WidgetExpressionV3.Text; nonPathBindingProblem names an unnamed widget by caption, suggests `Assoc/Attr or Module.Assoc/Attr` for a value with `/`, and drops the wrap-in-a-data-view advice inside a data container.
insight: When a value reaches a checker as an expression where a path was meant, look at the grammar alternative it fell out of before the checker: the generic `keyword: expression` fallback silently absorbs every near-miss of a specific property rule, and the checker then reports the symptom ("cannot hold the expression"), not the cause. The builder side needed no change — a builder test pinning qualified == bare AttributeRef guards it. Describe still prints the short form.
